title: AB503 (2019-2020): Gun-free school zone.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check, California); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text (Introduced 2019-02-13, via LegiScan getBillText)
provenance.note: No floor vote; saved text is the Introduced version of 2019-02-13 (last version). In (c)(5) the bill strikes the word 'who' and adds 'is'.

operative_text:
Section 626.9 (Penal Code): (c)(5) When the person holds a valid license to carry the firearm pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 26150) of Division 5 of Title 4 of Part 6, is carrying that firearm in an area that is not in, or on the grounds of, a public or private school providing instruction in kindergarten or grades 1 to 12, inclusive, but is within a distance of 1,000 feet from the grounds of the public or private school.
Section 626.9 (Penal Code): (c)(6) The person holds a valid license to carry the firearm pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 26150) of Division 5 of Title 4 of Part 6, is carrying the firearm to, from, or in a church, synagogue, or other building used as a place of worship on the grounds of a public school providing instruction in kindergarten or grades 1 to 12, inclusive, the person has the written permission of the school district superintendent, the superintendent’s designee, or equivalent school authority, and subject to the following: (A) A request for written permission may be denied. (B) The written permission shall be valid for no longer than one year. (C) The permission may be revoked at any time. (D) A person is only authorized to carry the firearm on school grounds pursuant to this paragraph during the time of worship.
Section 626.9 (Penal Code): (c)(7) The person holds a valid license to carry the firearm pursuant to Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 26150) of Division 5 of Title 4 of Part 6, is carrying the firearm to, from, or in a church, synagogue, or other building used as a place of worship on the grounds of a private school providing instruction in kindergarten or grades 1 to 12, inclusive, the person has the written permission of the school authority, and subject to the following: (A) A request for written permission may be denied. (B) The written permission shall be valid for no longer than the school authority specifies. (C) The permission may be revoked at any time. (D) A person is only authorized to carry the firearm on school grounds pursuant to this paragraph during the times specified by the school authority.
